title: eval-harness candidate contract, version 1
description: The wire contract between the harness and an HTTP candidate. The harness POSTs a request to the candidate's path (default /run) and reads one response. Version 1 is append-compatible only: a later version may add optional request or response fields, but no v1 field is removed, renamed, or given a new type. A server must ignore response fields it does not know; the harness ignores response fields it does not need. See docs/http-candidate.md.

request.title: Request
request.description: What the harness sends. prompt_override is null when the spec did not select a prompt variant. context is empty when the spec did not inject chunks. seed is the spec seed, repeated on every cell so the endpoint can be deterministic.

case_id.description: The case this cell runs; unique within one spec.

prompt.description: The case prompt exactly as the source supplied it.

context.description: Injected context chunks in spec order.

prompt_override.description: The resolved prompt variant, or null when there is none.

seed.description: The run seed. The same seed and case must give a deterministic answer if the endpoint claims determinism.

chunk_id.description: Stable identifier a citation can refer to.

response.title: Response
response.description: What the endpoint returns on HTTP 2xx. answer is the only required field. A missing usage object, or a missing token count, makes the harness estimate usage and record usage_source=estimated. Unknown fields are ignored.

answer.description: The candidate's answer. A wrong answer is a scored output, never an error and never a retry.

citations.description: Chunk ids or URLs the answer relies on, in the endpoint's own order.

usage.description: Provider-reported token counts. Omit it when the endpoint cannot report usage; the harness estimates instead.

tool_calls.description: How many tool calls the endpoint made for this case.

artifacts.description: Opaque JSON the endpoint wants recorded on the cell (trace ids, file paths, timings).

model.description: The model that answered, when it differs from the spec's candidate model. Optional; the spec model is the fallback.
